ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square, $BE \perp EF$, $DF \perp EF$, with $BE = 2.5 \, \text{dm}$, and $DF = 4 \, \text{dm}$. What is the length of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since ABCD is a square,\\
it follows that BC=CD, and BC$\perp$CD,\\
therefore, $\angle$BCE+$\angle$FCD=$90^\circ$,\\
also, since BE$\perp$EF and DF$\perp$EF,\\
it follows that $\angle$BEC=$\angle$CFD=$90^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$BCE+$\angle$EBC=$90^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle$EBC=$\angle$FCD,\\
hence, $\triangle$BEC$\cong$$\triangle$CFD,\\
therefore, BE=CF=2.5dm, and DF=EC=4dm,\\
thus, EF=EC+CF=$\boxed{6.5}$dm.

method.method_draft: Use triangle congruence around the two right triangles at the base. First read the figure: ABCD is drawn as a tilted square, E, C, F lie on one straight horizontal line, B is vertically above E, and D is vertically above F, so triangles BEC and CFD are the two right triangles on either side of C. From the text, use ABCD is a square, BE ⟂ EF, DF ⟂ EF, BE = 2.5 dm, DF = 4 dm. Since BC and CD are adjacent sides of the square, BC = CD and BC ⟂ CD. Because BE and DF are perpendicular to EF, ∠BEC and ∠CFD are right angles. The acute angles ∠EBC and ∠FCD are equal by complementary-angle reasoning from the right angle at C of the square. Therefore △BEC ≅ △CFD, so EC = DF = 4 dm and CF = BE = 2.5 dm. From the image C lies between E and F, hence EF = EC + CF = 4 + 2.5 = 6.5 dm.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/vector rotation model. First read the figure: EF is the horizontal baseline, C is on EF between E and F, BE is the vertical height from E to B, and DF is the vertical height from F to D. Let EC = x and CF = y. Then relative to C, vector CB has horizontal component -x and vertical component 2.5, while vector CD has horizontal component y and vertical component 4. From the text, ABCD is a square, so adjacent side vectors CB and CD have equal length and differ by a 90° rotation. The 90° rotation visible from CB to CD swaps the magnitude of the vertical component of CB into the horizontal component of CD and swaps the horizontal component of CB into the vertical component of CD. Thus y = BE = 2.5 and x = DF = 4. Since the figure shows E-C-F in order on one line, EF = EC + CF = x + y = 4 + 2.5 = 6.5 dm.
